body: STOP AND RE-ORDER before you go further into slice 1 - AuthorizedRemoteRequest (privacy.scala:772) and RemoteCapability (privacy.scala:743) go FIRST, ahead of ValidatedVector. My ordering was wrong and it mis-ranked the most severe site in the sweep. AuthorizedRemoteRequest's Scaladoc says 'the constructor is private so no code path can hand raw text to a remote provider'. fromProduct is such a code path, so that documented guarantee is false today: anyone can mint one with any payload and capability, bypassing RemotePolicy.evaluate's checks on provider allowlist, model identity, purpose, expiry, budget, detector identity and payload digest. That is the privacy boundary deciding whether participant-derived text leaves the machine, and it outranks arithmetic corruption. DEMONSTRATION DIFFERS for these two: not 'build an invalid value' but 'mint an authorization RemotePolicy.evaluate would have REFUSED' - forge a capability with a past expiry or an off-allowlist provider and show fromProduct produces it. WHY I GOT IT WRONG, so you can distrust the rest of my ordering appropriately: I ranked the 45 by whether the COMPANION held a smart constructor returning Either/Option. AuthorizedRemoteRequest has no companion at all - it is validated by RemotePolicy.evaluate, a different object - so my regex scored it 'not validating' and I ranked it below four arithmetic types. A search asking 'does this type validate itself' cannot see externally-gated types, and those are disproportionately the security-relevant ones. Your ValidatedVector reproduction was excellent and stands; just do these two before it.
